newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum-Buba concerned on prices, wants repo leeway.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum-Buba concerned on prices, wants repo leeway.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said the German central bank was concerned about signs of continued consumer price inflation, a German newspaper said on Thursday.
Gaddum also said in an interview with the daily Handelsblatt that the Bundesbank wanted leeway to act on its top money market rate, the securities repurchase rate, or repo.

"As regards our decisions we have to operate in a more uncertain environment and therefore want to retain full leeway in our Tuesday allocations," Gaddum said, referring to the Bundesbank's weekly repo tenders.
Gaddum's comments were reported in an advance release of an interview to be published on Friday.
Gaddum also reiterated the Bundesbank's often-repeated point that its monetary policy is not driven by developments on foreign exchange markets.
"We do not follow a concrete currency exchange rate goal, even though we naturally observe exaggerated moves very carefully," he said.
The weakening of the mark was relevant in so far as it affected economic developments. Continued increases in consumer prices on all fronts thus caused "some worries", he said.
Gaddum also said he believed the Bundesbank's expectation for inflation of 1.5 to two percent in 1997 was "entirely within reach."

The Bundesbank triggered an intense period of speculation about the course of its future policy last month when its policy makers left for their four-week summer holiday while deliberately leaving policy options open.
The central bank did not set a level for the repo for the full four week break, but only for the first two weeks.
The Handelsblatt said Gaddum maintained that the Bundesbank had broken with tradition because it wanted freedom to take faster action on the repo.
In the decision not to announce repo conditions in advance, the Bundesbank "applied a system again that we already did in the past."
